name: Bryn Shander
foundedNote: Approximate. The tenth and last of the towns, grown from a lone stopover cabin where traders began to gather in the late 1200s DR (Targos page). The Faerûn-level record uses 1080.

events.title: Battle of Icewind Dale
events.summary: Akar Kessell's goblin and giant host, driven by the Crystal Shard, besieges the town until Bruenor's dwarves and Wulfgar's united tribes break it.

events.title: Crystal Shard / barbarian assault
events.summary: The year Kessell stumbles on Crenshinibon, the Reghed tribes storm Ten-Towns and are routed at Bryn Shander's gates with Drizzt and Bruenor's help.

events.title: Everlasting Rime
events.summary: Auril's Everlasting Rime (begun 1486–1487) keeps the sun below the horizon; fires are doused and lotteries choose sacrifices until it lifts in 1489. Refugees from razed Good Mead and Dougan's Hole crowd inside the walls.

events.title: Errtu slain
events.summary: Tiago Baenre kills the returned demon Errtu on the plain outside town; a statue on a black circle marks the spot.

description: The hilltop hub of the dale sits apart from the three lakes, a ring of walls with three gates looking out over level snowfields toward Kelvin's Cairn. Every town's scrimshaw passes through its market square, and every caravan from beyond the Spine ends here. In hard times the eastern towns empty into it for shelter.

visual.notes: A round walled town crowning a single low hill in open snow, three gates and a crowded market square; no shoreline.

name: Targos
foundedNote: No founding date. Attested by 1281 DR (Speaker "K.T."); it predates Bryn Shander as the original end of the Ten Trail.

events.title: Burned by Cryshal-Tirith
events.summary: Kessell's tower fires a lance of focused sunlight across the lake, torching the walls and their watchers; his army then occupies the town while many flee by boat.

events.title: Siege of the Legion of the Chimera
events.summary: Goblinoid hordes besiege the palisade and slip in through old smugglers' tunnels; ships on the Shaengarne burn.

events.title: Elk tribe assault
events.summary: Speaker Kemp holds the town against the Tribe of the Elk in the barbarian rising of the Crystal Shard year.

events.title: Everlasting Rime
events.summary: Auril's Everlasting Rime (begun 1486–1487) keeps the sun below the horizon; fires are doused and lotteries choose sacrifices until it lifts in 1489. Speaker Naerth Maxildanarr, a Zhentarim agent, runs a lottery; the chardalyn dragon's attack is beaten back by militia and adventurers.

events.title: Black ice
events.summary: Chardalyn trinkets corrupt their owners while the Arcane Brotherhood angles for power in the council.

description: The second town of the dale crouches in a cliff-sheltered cove on Maer Dualdon, its timber palisade wading out into the lake to wall in the harbor. Its hundred-boat fleet out-fishes every rival, and shacks now spill beyond the walls as trade swells. The Ash Quarter, burned by Kessell's tower, has long since been built over.

visual.notes: Wooden palisade enclosing a cliff-backed cove and extending into the water as a harbor wall; a lighthouse and many fishing boats.

name: Termalaine
foundedNote: No founding date; first dated event is a goblin raid in 1342 DR. The name comes from its tourmaline mine.

events.title: Battle of Icewind Dale
events.summary: Kessell's orcs overrun the town; more than half the folk flee to Bryn Shander and Speaker Agorwal falls in the battle there.

events.title: Heafstaag's third attempt
events.summary: The barbarian king, who had taken Termalaine twice before, fails in the great rising of 1351.

events.title: Goblin raid
events.summary: Clan Battlehammer's dwarves save the town from goblin raiders.

events.title: Unnatural blizzard
events.summary: A magical storm empties the town and verbeeg move in until the Hero of Neverwinter drives them out.

events.title: Everlasting Rime
events.summary: Auril's Everlasting Rime (begun 1486–1487) keeps the sun below the horizon; fires are doused and lotteries choose sacrifices until it lifts in 1489.

description: Called the prettiest of the Ten Towns, Termalaine scatters its houses among planted trees on the eastern shore of Maer Dualdon, each behind a low rubble windbreak. Shipwrights and gem cutters work beside a tourmaline mine that opens and shuts with the moods of the Underdark. Its feud with Targos over fishing water has drawn blood more than once.

visual.notes: Widely spaced houses among small trees on a lakeshore, each behind a low stone wall; a mine mouth in a nearby rise.

name: Lonelywood
foundedNote: Circa 1232 DR: only logging camps then; the town grew around the Whistling Gallows inn and was recognized by the council shortly before 1281.

events.title: Wylfdene's war
events.summary: The barbarian king camps outside Lonelywood with three united tribes, aiming to drive the southerners from the dale; the campaign makes the hamlet a town.

events.title: Regis steps down
events.summary: After the barbarian rising the halfling Regis gives up the speaker's seat to Muldoon; the town's population swells.

events.title: Companions return
events.summary: Regis buys a house again; Catti-brie raises a small shrine to Mielikki in the woods.

events.title: Everlasting Rime
events.summary: Auril's Everlasting Rime (begun 1486–1487) keeps the sun below the horizon; fires are doused and lotteries choose sacrifices until it lifts in 1489.

description: The northernmost town hides among the fir stands of the Lonelywood on Maer Dualdon, a few dozen low log cabins where people come to vanish. It cuts the timber every other town builds with. Hunters share their kills with the whole community, and the old tree outside the Whistling Gallows is carved with visitors' names.

visual.notes: A cluster of log cabins inside a dark fir wood at the lake's north end; one great carved tree by an inn.

name: Bremen
foundedNote: Founded by dwarven prospectors under Rölph Bremen; undated. Earliest dated event is its near-destruction by the Legion of the Chimera just before 1312 DR.

events.title: Legion of the Chimera
events.summary: The goblinoid Legion nearly wipes out the westernmost town just before its siege of Targos.

events.title: Given to the Reghedmen
events.summary: After the war with Kessell, Bremen is handed to the barbarian tribes; Revjak of the Elk speaks for them until Berkthgar's challenge in 1364.

events.title: Everlasting Rime
events.summary: Bremen offers up warmth to Auril, going a day a month without fire; an awakened plesiosaur stalks Maer Dualdon's boats.

description: Westernmost of the lake towns, Bremen sits where the Shaengarne pours into Maer Dualdon, on ground the spring floods know well. Prospectors still pan the river flats for gold, and a statue of the dwarf who founded the place stands in its heart. It is small, poor, and could muster barely two dozen defenders during the Rime.

visual.notes: A small huddle of houses at a river mouth on a lakeshore with a central dwarf statue; flat flood-prone banks.

name: Easthaven
foundedNote: Founded by thieves fleeing Cape Velen in Tethyr; undated. Earliest dated event 1281 DR.

events.title: Crystal Shard
events.summary: Akar Kessell murders his master Morkai the Red at Easthaven, then is left in the snow and finds Crenshinibon.

events.title: Belhifet's tower
events.summary: The devil Belhifet raises a crystal tower over the town with Crenshinibon, trying to open a gate to the Hells beneath the Tempuran chapel; adventurers defeat him.

events.title: Glensather falls
events.summary: Easthaven's speaker dies fighting orcs in the Battle of Icewind Dale.

events.title: Chardalyn dragon
events.summary: Auril's Everlasting Rime (begun 1486–1487) keeps the sun below the horizon; fires are doused and lotteries choose sacrifices until it lifts in 1489. Xardorok Sunblight's dragon smashes a trench through the town before adventurers bring it down.

events.title: Pirate raid
events.summary: Raiders of the Howling Fiend strike the armory as part of the risen Kessell's scheming.

description: Easthaven grew from a shanty into the busiest port on Lac Dinneshere once the Eastway was paved to Bryn Shander. A breakwater shelters its piers and ferries, its inns are the most comfortable in the dale, and its people joke that anything goes here. A furrow carved by a falling chardalyn dragon still scars the middle of town.

visual.notes: A spreading lakeside town with a long breakwater and piers; a white tower motif from its crest; a scar trench through the middle.

name: Caer-Dineval
foundedNote: The Dinev family of Cormyr built the castle in 1050 DR; Ten Towns began from their community on Lac Dinneshere.

events.title: The Dinev castle
events.summary: Exiles from Cormyr raise a stone keep on the Cliffs of Dinev, meaning to claim the whole dale.

events.title: Orc siege
events.summary: Orcs wipe out the settlement; the starving Dinevs fall when the castle is breached.

events.title: Retaken
events.summary: About a decade later the ancestors of the present townsfolk drive the orcs out of the castle (c.).

events.title: Everlasting Rime
events.summary: Auril's Everlasting Rime (begun 1486–1487) keeps the sun below the horizon; fires are doused and lotteries choose sacrifices until it lifts in 1489.

description: Caer-Dineval curls in a half-moon around Knucklehead Harbor on Lac Dinneshere, its old stone castle looking down from the cliffs to the east. The speaker lives in the Caer. A fishing pact with Caer-Konig holds only because both fear Easthaven's fleet more than each other.

visual.notes: A crescent of houses around a round harbor with a small stone castle on a cliff above it.

name: Caer-Konig
foundedNote: Began as a camp of mountain climbers from the Moonsea; undated. Earliest dated record is the council of 1351 DR.

events.title: Given to the Reghedmen
events.summary: After Kessell's defeat the town is handed to the barbarians; Revjak serves as their speaker until 1364.

events.title: Killed over a fish
events.summary: Speaker Dorim Lugar is slain in a fishing quarrel (by 1356); the heavy-handed Schermont replaces him.

events.title: Everlasting Rime
events.summary: The town offers food to Auril; duergar under Nildar Sunblight commit a string of thefts.

description: The northernmost town on Lac Dinneshere lies in the shadow of Kelvin's Cairn, a semicircle of houses climbing a slope above a round harbor. Its only links are a trail to Caer-Dineval and a ferry to Easthaven. A castle once stood here, but orcs threw it down long ago.

visual.notes: Houses in a ring on a slope above a round harbor, a broken castle stump nearby, a lone mountain looming behind.

name: Good Mead
foundedNote: Undated; first appears on the council roll of 1351 DR.

events.title: Razed by the chardalyn dragon
events.summary: In under an hour Xardorok Sunblight's dragon flattens every building except the Mead Hall; survivors flee to Bryn Shander.

events.title: Fish turns to mead
events.summary: By the mid-1300s Redwaters yields little profit and the town turns to brewing the mead it is named for (c.).

events.title: Everlasting Rime
events.summary: Auril's endless winter falls over the dale (c. 1486–1487).

description: Good Mead sat on the northwest shore of Redwaters, a small town that gave up on thin fishing to brew the honey wine sold in Bryn Shander's market. During the Rime a chardalyn dragon reduced it to rubble around its lone surviving mead hall. Its rivalry with Dougan's Hole is old and only half-forgiven.

visual.notes: A tiny lakeside hamlet around a single large timber mead hall; after 1489 the rest is rubble.

name: Dougan's Hole
foundedNote: Founded by the fisher Dougan Dubrace; undated. First appears on the council roll of 1351 DR.

events.title: Razed by the chardalyn dragon
events.summary: In half an hour the dragon destroys every structure and kills 25 people, sparing only the Twenty Stones of Thruun; Speaker Durmoot leads survivors to Bryn Shander.

events.title: Everlasting Rime
events.summary: The town sacrifices its fires to Auril; ice locks the shore hundreds of yards out and ruins both piers.

events.title: Winter wolves
events.summary: The winter wolves Koran and Kanan extort and abduct townsfolk.

description: The smallest and most closed-off of the Ten Towns is a handful of buildings by two piers on the west shore of Redwaters, its streets laid with gravel against the mud. Its people cut holes in the ice to fish and openly honor Auril. Strangers are tolerated for a day or two, and never welcomed.

visual.notes: A few huts by one long and one short pier on a frozen lake; a ring of old standing stones nearby.

name: Kelvin's Cairn
foundedNote: Geography. Reghed legend says Tempus heaped the rocks over the slain frost giant Kelvin.

events.title: Kessell's last stand
events.summary: Atop the Cairn Kessell calls up fire with Crenshinibon, melting the snows; he dies by his own spell and the avalanche buries his tower.

events.title: Kessell's corpse found
events.summary: A Luskan expedition finds the wizard risen as a wight near the summit; he spreads corrupting black ice through the mines below.

events.title: Drizzt's cave
events.summary: Sent there by Cassius, Drizzt Do'Urden makes a sparse home in a cave on the barren north face (c.).

description: The only peak for a thousand square miles rises alone between the lakes, a thousand-foot heap of loose boulders under year-round snow. Reghedmen say a god piled it over a dead frost giant. Verbeeg, yetis, and remorhazes den in its crags, and its north face once sheltered a lone drow ranger.

visual.notes: A single steep snow-capped boulder pile rising from flat tundra, a deep valley cut along its south flank.

name: Reghed Glacier
foundedNote: Geography. The Reghedmen claim Dawn Age giants raised it to mark their border.

events.title: Icingdeath slain
events.summary: Drizzt and Wulfgar kill the white dragon in his lair under the Evermelt springs when Aegis-fang brings down a great icicle on him.

events.title: The tribes take its name
events.summary: Illuskan refugees settle the dale; their descendants, the Reghedmen, are named for the glacier.

events.title: Everlasting Rime
events.summary: The dale's eastern edge is among the harshest stretches of Auril's endless winter (c. 1486–1489).

description: A wall of ancient ice fences Icewind Dale on the east, so bleak that few dare even its edges. Beyond it lies frozen waste and then the Endless Ice Sea. The barbarian tribes of the dale take their name from it, and hot springs at Evermelt once hid a white dragon's hoard.

visual.notes: A long low cliff of blue-white ice along one edge of the board, with a steaming spring at its foot.

name: Sea of Moving Ice

events.title: The Ostorian spindle
events.summary: Arcanists of the Netherese enclave Ythryn find an ancient stone spindle in the ice.

events.title: Auril's island
events.summary: The Frostmaiden, at odds with Umberlee, hides on the isle of Solstice and casts the Everlasting Rime from there each night (c. 1486–1489).

events.title: Ambergris hunter
events.summary: Waterdhavian whaler Jendren Uruth makes regular runs among the bergs in the late 1480s (c.).

description: North and west of the dale, drifting bergs and frosted isles crowd a cold sea that refuses to stay charted. Ships older than memory sit locked in the ice. Seals, walruses, and polar bears share it with ice trolls in old wrecks and white dragons in hollow bergs; Reghedmen call it the Floating Land and mostly shun it.

visual.notes: Dark water crowded with white icebergs of many sizes, one frozen-in shipwreck.

name: Dwarven Valley
foundedNote: Approximate. Clan Battlehammer survivors settled here after fleeing Mithral Hall in the late 1100s DR (Mithral Hall record uses c. 1190).

events.title: Tunnels collapsed
events.summary: The dwarves lure Kessell's army into their southern passages and bring the rock down on it.

events.title: Return to Mithral Hall
events.summary: Many Battlehammers leave to resettle their ancestral hall after Bruenor reclaims it (c.).

events.title: Black ice schism
events.summary: Remnants of Cryshal-Tirith fused into the ice corrupt miners; the community splits between Stokely Silverstream and Baerick Hammerstone while the wight Kessell raises dwarf zombies below.

events.title: Exiles arrive
events.summary: Battlehammer survivors of Shimmergloom's attack settle under Kelvin's Cairn and trade arms to Ten-Towns (c.).

description: A deep rift along the southern foot of Kelvin's Cairn holds two dwarven halls cut into facing walls, each with its forge at the heart. Mines branch out beyond, some worked out and some seeded with black ice from Kessell's shattered tower. Their iron weapons fill Bryn Shander's shops.

visual.notes: A narrow gorge with two carved dwarf gates in opposite cliff walls, forge glow inside, mine mouths beyond.
